problem_statement: The socket service API has no way to tell a registered pollable socket to be closed by the service itself when it stops polling. A caller that unregisters a service (net_socket_service_unregister) leaves the underlying socket open and is unable to know when it is safe to close it, because the socket service may still be polling it. There must be an API (net_socket_service_close) that unregisters the pollable sockets and additionally causes the socket service to close them for the caller; after calling it the caller's own close() on that socket must then fail because the socket has already been closed. The sntp_close_async helper must also defer the socket close to the socket service instead of closing it while it is being polled.
